sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
- This course aims to expand the understanding of research in life science and help freshmen to acquire basic research capabilities by participating in research at life science laboratories to conduct experiments and practical training.
- Students will participate in on-going research projects currently taking place in the labs to learn basic experimental techniques and experience the research process step-by-step, ranging from hypothesis formulation and experimental design to data interpretation.
- After the course registration, students' areas of interest are surveyed to match them with the available capacity of the laboratories, after which assignments are made.
- In the assigned laboratories, students participate in experimental activities under the guidance of professors and research mentors, and submit the results of their activities in the form of a final report.
- Through the course, students can gain a practical sense of how research in life science labs is conducted, develop basic experimental skills, and have valuable research experience that will help explore a diverse set of disciplines and develop their future scientific careers.

※ 관련 참고사항: 학기별 POVIS 교내회보 안내문(Off-Campus(OC) 학기제 신청 안내)을 참고
※ OC 학기제 이수를 위한 필수 조건 아님(선택하여 이수 가능)
※ 본 교과목(Off-Campus 프로그램)의 최종 이수 결과가 낙제(U)일 경우, OC 학기제 장학금 환수 대상(전액, 100%)에 해당함에 유의
※ 동일한 활동 내역에 대해 중복하여 본 교과목의 학점으로 인정받을 수 없음에 유의

- 비교과 활동 마일리지(PAM)를 부여받는 경우(봉사활동/교외 공모전·경진대회 참여 등)에도, 본 교과목 이수와 중복 인정 불가함.
※ 학점 이수를 위한 교내 기준 및 가이드: “강좌 수강 기준 90시간 / 실습 등의 경우 180시간” 이수 시 6학점 인정
*학칙 제29조(학점) 교과이수의 단위는 학점으로 하고 1학기간 15시간 이상의 수업을 1학점으로 한다.
다만, 실험·실습, 체육 기타 총장이 정하는 과목은 1학기 30시간 이상의 수업을 1학점으로 한다.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
*구, 확률시스템분석과 동일과목임
This course was formerly known as Probability Modeling & Analysis (IMEN366). This course covers basic modeling tools to handle stochastic systems such as Markov Chains, Poisson processes, Continuous-Time Markov Chains, renewal theory, and queueing theory. Some of reliability theory is also covered.
sourceOperatingSections.4. 강의선수/수강필수사항: IMEN 272 (Probability and Statistics for Engineers) or MATH 230 (Probability and Statistics)
sourceOperatingSections.8. 강의진도계획:
Week 1-2 Chapter 1-3: Basic Probability
- Probability of events, conditional probability, law of total probability, random variables, distributions, moments, multi-variate, etc
Week 3-5 Chapter 4: Markov Chains
- Definitions, transition probabilities, transition diagrams, modeling, transient analysis, classification of states, steady-state analysis, etc.
Week 6-8 Chapter 5-6: Continuous-time Markov Chains
- Exponential distributions, Poisson process, Markov processes, states, generator matrix, rate diagram, modeling, transient analysis, steady-state analysis, costs and rewards, etc.
Week 9-11 Chapter 7: Renewal Theory
- Renewal process, limit theorems, Regenerative process, Semi-Markov process, Inspection paradox, etc.
Week 12-14 Chapter 8: Queueing Theory
- Nomenclature, Markovian queues (M/M/s/k type queues), general queues, Jackson network of queues, multi-class queues, etc
Week 15-16 Chapter 9: Reliability Theory
- Structure functions, Reliability functions, System lifetime, etc

The objective of this course is to introduce the recent topics in financial engineering, focusing on the basic theories of financial derivative pricing, portfolio management, and financial risk management, and their applications (e.g., patent valuation). For this, we explore:
1. the basic theory of interest rates and financial derivative pricing,
2. its applications to real assets (e.g., patent valuation),
3. the basic theory of financial risk management,
4. the basic theory of portfolio theory, and
5. Fintech businesses or ML modelling in Finance.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
The pace of change in the business environment is faster today than ever before in that new technologies and innovations force industries and firms to find new ways to compete and survive. As a practical matter, this rapid pace of change has resulted in an increasing number of engineers and technicians moving beyond technology concerns into management. To meet these demands, a business has been required to manage organizational tasks for technology and innovation productively. To do so, however, is greatly challenging to the most of people who never thought they would need to understand the intricacies of managing technology and innovation.
The strategic management of technological innovation (SMTI), therefore, become a fundamental issue that faces all technology-intensive firms today. In this course, we will explore the strategic approaches to SMTI in the course designed to serve as a managerial guide for technical professionals and business practitioners. This type of approach is needed for engineering and science/technology-based students, providing an integrated view of technology/innovation which interacts with external and internal environments.
This course was developed to meet several goals:
1) To integrate strategy and technology/innovation
2) To make the theoretical and practical understanding of SMTI
3) To provide insight into SMTI as an applied discipline that students are able to use.
4) To learn strategic analyzing tools for building up the technological competitive advantage

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
Marketing is no longer limited to selling products; it is a strategic discipline that creates customer value through data, technology, and innovation. This course introduces the fundamental principles of marketing while emphasizing their application in technology-driven industries.
Designed primarily for engineering students, the course bridges technological innovation and business strategy by helping students understand customer needs, develop market-oriented solutions, and communicate technological value effectively.
Students will learn how successful firms identify market opportunities, design customer value propositions, build strong brands, develop pricing strategies, manage distribution channels, and implement integrated marketing communications. Throughout the semester, students will analyze real-world business cases and work in teams to evaluate the marketing strategies of domestic and global companies.
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Understand the fundamental concepts and frameworks of modern marketing, including customer value creation, STP (Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning), and the marketing mix (4Ps).
2. Analyze customer needs, buying behavior, and market environments using qualitative and quantitative information.
3. Develop customer-oriented marketing strategies for technology-based products and services.
4. Evaluate branding, pricing, distribution, and marketing communication strategies from a managerial perspective.
5. Apply marketing concepts to engineering and technology commercialization.
6. Critically analyze the marketing strategies and competitive advantages of real companies.
7. Improve teamwork, presentation, and business communication skills through group projects and discussions.

- Understand graphs, graph traversal and paths within graphs

- Implement the algorithms covered by this course in Python
- Design and evaluate efficient algorithms in Python to solve specific applied problems

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
본 교과목은 스타트업/사내벤처 비즈니스의 성공 핵심 요인(Critical Sucess Factor)인 증거 기반 기업가정신(Evidence-based Entrepreneurship) 방법론을 학습하는데 목적이 있습니다.
기업가정신의 핵심 활동은 밸류에이션 증진을 위한 신사업개발/신제품 개발 활동이며, 이러한 신사업개발/신제품개발 활동은 기업이 존재하는 이유(Reason for Beign)를 설명합니다.
하지만 모든 비즈니스 프로젝트가 항상 성공적인 건 아닙니다. 무수히 많은 실패를 거치게 됩니다. 프로젝트 실패는 결국 매몰비용(Sunk Cost)로 전락하여, 기업에 돌이킬 수 없는 큰 타격을 입힙니다.
이리하여 경영학에서는 실패를 줄이기 위한 여러 방법론 연구가 진행되어 왔습니다. 그 결과, 고객발굴(Customer Discovery)과 린스타트업(Lean Startup)으로 구성된 증거 기반 기업가정신이 가장 효과적인 방법론으로 확인되었습니다.
고객발굴 프로세스는 (1) 제안한 비즈니스 컨셉의 기저를 이루는 '시장/고객에 대한 가정'을 '비즈니스 가설'로 수립하여, (2) 잠재 고객을 만나 직접 대화를 나누는 고객인터뷰를 통해서 가설을 검증할 증거 자료를 수집하고, (3) 증거 자료를 분석하고 패턴화하여 가설을 검증함으로써 (4) 비즈니스가 시장에 존재해야 하는 이유를 규명하는 것입니다.
이러한 증거 기반 활동을 통해서 시장성이 없는 비즈니스 컨셉로 판명되면, 관련 프로세스를 중단(Stop)합니다.
시장성이 높다고 판명된 비즈니스 컨셉은 린스타트업을 위한 고객발굴을 진행합니다. 린스타트업의 핵심은 MVP(Minimum Viable Product, 최소요건제품) 개발입니다. MVP는 고객이 여러분의 비즈니스 컨셉에서 진정으로 원하는 것, 즉 고객가치를 의미합니다. 이를 위해선 다시 인터뷰를 통해 MVP와 관련된 가설을 검증하는 고객발굴 활동을 수행해야 합니다.
모든 혁신 선도 기업들이 위 활동을 수행하는 만큼, 본 교과목을 통해 고객발굴 & 린스타트업 방법론을 학습/이해하시면 향후 여러분이 실무 활동에서 가치 창출을 이끌 혁신적 기업가(Innovative Entrepreneur)로 거듭날 수 있습니다.
수강자 여러분께서는 한 학기 동안 저와 증거 기반 기업가정신 활동을 수행할 것입니다. 자, 이제 우리와 함께 기업가적 여정(Entrepreneurial Journey)을 떠나 볼까요?

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
Entrepreneurship is increasingly recognized as one of the most essential competencies for engineers, scientists, and future business leaders. In today's rapidly changing technological environment, entrepreneurial thinking is critical not only for starting new ventures but also for driving innovation within established organizations.
This course introduces the fundamental concepts, frameworks, and processes of entrepreneurship, with particular emphasis on technology-based innovation. Students will learn how entrepreneurs recognize opportunities, evaluate business ideas, develop business models, acquire resources, build entrepreneurial teams, and launch new ventures.
The course combines conceptual learning with experiential team projects. Working in interdisciplinary teams, students will identify real-world problems, generate innovative solutions, validate customer needs, develop business models, and present venture proposals through a final pitch presentation.
The course is designed primarily for engineering students who wish to develop entrepreneurial thinking regardless of whether they intend to start a company in the future.
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Explain the role of entrepreneurship in economic development, technological innovation, and societal impact.
2. Recognize entrepreneurial opportunities through systematic opportunity identification and customer discovery.
3. Evaluate the feasibility of new venture ideas using market, industry, technical, and financial analyses.
4. Design sustainable business models using contemporary entrepreneurial frameworks.
5. Understand entrepreneurial finance, venture capital, intellectual property, and startup growth strategies.
6. Develop leadership, teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills through collaborative projects.
7. Prepare and deliver professional venture pitches supported by market analysis and business model validation.
8. Apply entrepreneurial thinking to engineering, technology commercialization, and innovation management.
9. Understand how emerging technologies—including AI, digital platforms, and sustainability—are reshaping entrepreneurial opportunities.

"기업가정신과 기술혁신" 수업의 목표는 이공계 대학생들이 기업가정신과 기술혁신의 중요성을 인식하고, 창의적인 문제해결 능력을 갖추며, 사회적 가치 창출을 위한 혁신적인 아이디어를 만들어내는 능력을 키우는 것입니다. 이를 위해 다음과 같은 내용을 학습 합니다.
- 기업가정신: 기업가정신이란 창의적인 문제해결 능력, 기회 인식 능력, 실행력, 혁신성, 그리고 실패에 대한 대처 능력 등을 의미합니다. 이러한 기업가정신을 개발하고 기업가정신의 중요성을 이해할 수 있습니다.
- 기술혁신: 기술혁신은 새로운 아이디어, 제품, 서비스, 프로세스 등을 만들어내는 것을 의미합니다. 기술혁신의 중요성과 혁신 아이디어를 만들어내는 방법을 배울 수 있습니다.
- 창업 및 경영: 창업 및 경영에 필요한 기본적인 지식을 습득하고, 비즈니스 모델, 마케팅, 자금 조달 등을 이해할 수 있습니다.
- 기술과 사회문제 해결: 기술을 사용하여 사회문제를 해결하는 방법을 배울 수 있습니다. 이를 통해 사회적 가치 창출과 기술적 혁신이 결합된 결과를 얻을 수 있습니다.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
What is entrepreneurship, and what, why, and how to innovate? 우리는 급변하는 환경 속에서 생존과 성공을 위해 개인과 조직의 새로운 가치를 창출해야 하는 기업가적 혁신(entrepreneurial innovation)의 시대를 살아가고 있다. 하지만 우리 중 대다수는 개인과 조직이 세상에 존재해야 하는 이유(the reason for being)를 입증하는데 필요한 기업가적 혁신이 무엇이며 어떻게 수행해야 하는지에 대해서 제대로 알지 못한다.
초경쟁의 환경 속에서 우리는 수많은 기회와 위협을 마주하고 있으며, 이에 따라 기존의 방식으로는 경쟁우위를 확보하거나 유지하기 어렵다. ‘기회 인식’, ‘문제 해결’, 그리고 ‘자원 활용’의 기업가적 활동으로 이루어진 기업가정신(entrepreneurship)은 환경 변화에 따라 출현하는 새로운 가치 창출 기회의 포착과 실현에 따른 문제를 해결하고, 이에 필요한 자원을 기존과 다른 새로운 방식으로 결합하는 혁신 사고와 태도를 결정한다. 즉, 경쟁우위의 원천인 혁신을 이끄는 기업가정신은 개인과 조직인 변화에 대응하고 자신의 가치를 입증하기 위해 반드시 함양해야 할 삶의 기술(like skill)이다.
이처럼 기업가정신의 필요성은 모든 이들에게 강조되지만, 누구에게나 보편적이고 일률적으로 적용 가능한 기업가적 프로세스(entrepreneurial process)는 존재하지 않는다. 모두가 동일 목표를 향해 동일 방법을 취한다면, 누구도 차별화할 수 없고 경쟁력을 가질 수 없기 때문이다. 따라서 기업가정신은 그 행동 주체인 기업가의 특성, 환경 및 자원 등의 특수 요인에 따라서 다른 의미와 접근이 필요하다. 이것이 바로 성공한 기업가들이 동일 기회에 대하여 서로 다른 혁신 접근을 취하는 이유이다.
이를 위해 우리는 자신이 누구이고, 어떠한 자원과 역량을 갖고 있으며, 어떠한 환경에 둘러싸여 있는지에 대한 정확한 분석을 바탕으로 가치 창출 전략을 설계하는 기업가적 여정(entrepreneurial journey)을 떠나야 한다. 자신에 대한 이해를 기반으로 올바른 비전과 목표를 설정하고, 이를 달성하기 위해 현재 상태와 기대 상태의 차이를 좁혀가는 자신만의 차별화된 기업가적 프로세스를 설계해야 한다.
이에 본 교과목은 개인과 조직의 가치 증명과 경쟁우위 개발을 위한 접근법으로써 기업가정신과 혁신에 대한 수강자의 이해 증진과 역량 개발을 주요 학습 목표로 제시한다. 우선, 관련 이론과 사례에 관한 교수 강의를 통해 기업가의 행동 및 사고 특성을 살펴보고, 각자가 전공 과정에서 기업가적 혁신을 수행할 수 있도록 증거기반 기업가정신(evidence-based entrepreneurship)에 관한 체계적 기법을 액션러닝을 통해 학습한다. 본 교과목은 기업가적 활동의 일차적 초점을 신사업개발(new business development)에 맞추고 있다. 그러나 개인 차원의 가치 창출도 간과할 수 없는 주요 주제이므로, 퍼스널 비즈니스 모델(personal business model)의 설계 방법을 학습하는데 이차적 초점을 두고 있다. 본 과목은 수강자가 향후 개별 전공에서 습득할 이공학적 지식 및 역량을 활용하여 가치 창출을 이끌 혁신을 주도할 창조적 기업가로 성장할 수 있도록 관련 기반을 제공한다. 주요 학습 활동은 다음과 같다.
1) 기회 인식, 문제 해결 및 자원 활용에 관한 기업가적 활동 역량 개발
2) 사회 문제 해결을 위한 창의적 솔루션의 비즈니스 모델 개발
3) 신사업개발 방법론과 시장 검증 방법론에 대한 이해
4) 퍼스널 비즈니스 모델을 통한 개인적 가치 창출 기회 탐색

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
"기업가정신과 기술혁신" 수업의 목표는 이공계 대학생들이 기업가정신과 기술혁신의 중요성을 인식하고, 창의적인 문제해결 능력을 갖추며, 사회적 가치 창출을 위한 혁신적인 아이디어를 만들어내는 능력을 키우는 것입니다. 이를 위해 다음과 같은 내용을 학습 합니다.
- 기업가정신: 기업가정신이란 창의적인 문제해결 능력, 기회 인식 능력, 실행력, 혁신성, 그리고 실패에 대한 대처 능력 등을 의미합니다. 이러한 기업가정신을 개발하고 기업가정신의 중요성을 이해할 수 있습니다.
- 기술혁신: 기술혁신은 새로운 아이디어, 제품, 서비스, 프로세스 등을 만들어내는 것을 의미합니다. 기술혁신의 중요성과 혁신 아이디어를 만들어내는 방법을 배울 수 있습니다.
- 창업 및 경영: 창업 및 경영에 필요한 기본적인 지식을 습득하고, 비즈니스 모델, 마케팅, 자금 조달 등을 이해할 수 있습니다.
- 기술과 사회문제 해결: 기술을 사용하여 사회문제를 해결하는 방법을 배울 수 있습니다. 이를 통해 사회적 가치 창출과 기술적 혁신이 결합된 결과를 얻을 수 있습니다.

- 교과목 수강생은 지식재산 인식제고의 일환으로 교과/비교과 프로그램에 자유롭게 참여할 수 있으며, 심화학습이 필요한 경우 산업경영학과 행정팀 (279-3817)로 연락 바랍니다.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
What is entrepreneurship, and what, why, and how to innovate? 우리는 급변하는 환경 속에서 생존과 성공을 위해 개인과 조직의 새로운 가치를 창출해야 하는 기업가적 혁신(entrepreneurial innovation)의 시대를 살아가고 있다. 하지만 우리 중 대다수는 개인과 조직이 세상에 존재해야 하는 이유(the reason for being)를 입증하는데 필요한 기업가적 혁신이 무엇이며 어떻게 수행해야 하는지에 대해서 제대로 알지 못한다.
초경쟁의 환경 속에서 우리는 수많은 기회와 위협을 마주하고 있으며, 이에 따라 기존의 방식으로는 경쟁우위를 확보하거나 유지하기 어렵다. ‘기회 인식’, ‘문제 해결’, 그리고 ‘자원 활용’의 기업가적 활동으로 이루어진 기업가정신(entrepreneurship)은 환경 변화에 따라 출현하는 새로운 가치 창출 기회의 포착과 실현에 따른 문제를 해결하고, 이에 필요한 자원을 기존과 다른 새로운 방식으로 결합하는 혁신 사고와 태도를 결정한다. 즉, 경쟁우위의 원천인 혁신을 이끄는 기업가정신은 개인과 조직인 변화에 대응하고 자신의 가치를 입증하기 위해 반드시 함양해야 할 삶의 기술(like skill)이다.
이처럼 기업가정신의 필요성은 모든 이들에게 강조되지만, 누구에게나 보편적이고 일률적으로 적용 가능한 기업가적 프로세스(entrepreneurial process)는 존재하지 않는다. 모두가 동일 목표를 향해 동일 방법을 취한다면, 누구도 차별화할 수 없고 경쟁력을 가질 수 없기 때문이다. 따라서 기업가정신은 그 행동 주체인 기업가의 특성, 환경 및 자원 등의 특수 요인에 따라서 다른 의미와 접근이 필요하다. 이것이 바로 성공한 기업가들이 동일 기회에 대하여 서로 다른 혁신 접근을 취하는 이유이다.
이를 위해 우리는 자신이 누구이고, 어떠한 자원과 역량을 갖고 있으며, 어떠한 환경에 둘러싸여 있는지에 대한 정확한 분석을 바탕으로 가치 창출 전략을 설계하는 기업가적 여정(entrepreneurial journey)을 떠나야 한다. 자신에 대한 이해를 기반으로 올바른 비전과 목표를 설정하고, 이를 달성하기 위해 현재 상태와 기대 상태의 차이를 좁혀가는 자신만의 차별화된 기업가적 프로세스를 설계해야 한다.
이에 본 교과목은 개인과 조직의 가치 증명과 경쟁우위 개발을 위한 접근법으로써 기업가정신과 혁신에 대한 수강자의 이해 증진과 역량 개발을 주요 학습 목표로 제시한다. 우선, 관련 이론과 사례에 관한 교수 강의를 통해 기업가의 행동 및 사고 특성을 살펴보고, 각자가 전공 과정에서 기업가적 혁신을 수행할 수 있도록 증거기반 기업가정신(evidence-based entrepreneurship)에 관한 체계적 기법을 액션러닝을 통해 학습한다. 본 교과목은 기업가적 활동의 일차적 초점을 신사업개발(new business development)에 맞추고 있다. 그러나 개인 차원의 가치 창출도 간과할 수 없는 주요 주제이므로, 퍼스널 비즈니스 모델(personal business model)의 설계 방법을 학습하는데 이차적 초점을 두고 있다. 본 과목은 수강자가 향후 개별 전공에서 습득할 이공학적 지식 및 역량을 활용하여 가치 창출을 이끌 혁신을 주도할 창조적 기업가로 성장할 수 있도록 관련 기반을 제공한다. 주요 학습 활동은 다음과 같다.
1) 기회 인식, 문제 해결 및 자원 활용에 관한 기업가적 활동 역량 개발
2) 사회 문제 해결을 위한 창의적 솔루션의 비즈니스 모델 개발
3) 신사업개발 방법론과 시장 검증 방법론에 대한 이해
4) 퍼스널 비즈니스 모델을 통한 개인적 가치 창출 기회 탐색

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
Entrepreneurship is increasingly recognized as one of the most essential competencies for engineers, scientists, and future business leaders. In today's rapidly changing technological environment, entrepreneurial thinking is critical not only for starting new ventures but also for driving innovation within established organizations.
This course introduces the fundamental concepts, frameworks, and processes of entrepreneurship, with particular emphasis on technology-based innovation. Students will learn how entrepreneurs recognize opportunities, evaluate business ideas, develop business models, acquire resources, build entrepreneurial teams, and launch new ventures.
The course combines conceptual learning with experiential team projects. Working in interdisciplinary teams, students will identify real-world problems, generate innovative solutions, validate customer needs, develop business models, and present venture proposals through a final pitch presentation.
The course is designed primarily for engineering students who wish to develop entrepreneurial thinking regardless of whether they intend to start a company in the future.
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Explain the role of entrepreneurship in economic development, technological innovation, and societal impact.
2. Recognize entrepreneurial opportunities through systematic opportunity identification and customer discovery.
3. Evaluate the feasibility of new venture ideas using market, industry, technical, and financial analyses.
4. Design sustainable business models using contemporary entrepreneurial frameworks.
5. Understand entrepreneurial finance, venture capital, intellectual property, and startup growth strategies.
6. Develop leadership, teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills through collaborative projects.
7. Prepare and deliver professional venture pitches supported by market analysis and business model validation.
8. Apply entrepreneurial thinking to engineering, technology commercialization, and innovation management.
9. Understand how emerging technologies—including AI, digital platforms, and sustainability—are reshaping entrepreneurial opportunities.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
본 교과목은 스타트업/사내벤처 비즈니스의 성공 핵심 요인(Critical Sucess Factor)인 증거 기반 기업가정신(Evidence-based Entrepreneurship) 방법론을 학습하는데 목적이 있습니다.
기업가정신의 핵심 활동은 밸류에이션 증진을 위한 신사업개발/신제품 개발 활동이며, 이러한 신사업개발/신제품개발 활동은 기업이 존재하는 이유(Reason for Beign)를 설명합니다.
하지만 모든 비즈니스 프로젝트가 항상 성공적인 건 아닙니다. 무수히 많은 실패를 거치게 됩니다. 프로젝트 실패는 결국 매몰비용(Sunk Cost)로 전락하여, 기업에 돌이킬 수 없는 큰 타격을 입힙니다.
이리하여 경영학에서는 실패를 줄이기 위한 여러 방법론 연구가 진행되어 왔습니다. 그 결과, 고객발굴(Customer Discovery)과 린스타트업(Lean Startup)으로 구성된 증거 기반 기업가정신이 가장 효과적인 방법론으로 확인되었습니다.
고객발굴 프로세스는 (1) 제안한 비즈니스 컨셉의 기저를 이루는 '시장/고객에 대한 가정'을 '비즈니스 가설'로 수립하여, (2) 잠재 고객을 만나 직접 대화를 나누는 고객인터뷰를 통해서 가설을 검증할 증거 자료를 수집하고, (3) 증거 자료를 분석하고 패턴화하여 가설을 검증함으로써 (4) 비즈니스가 시장에 존재해야 하는 이유를 규명하는 것입니다.
이러한 증거 기반 활동을 통해서 시장성이 없는 비즈니스 컨셉로 판명되면, 관련 프로세스를 중단(Stop)합니다.
시장성이 높다고 판명된 비즈니스 컨셉은 린스타트업을 위한 고객발굴을 진행합니다. 린스타트업의 핵심은 MVP(Minimum Viable Product, 최소요건제품) 개발입니다. MVP는 고객이 여러분의 비즈니스 컨셉에서 진정으로 원하는 것, 즉 고객가치를 의미합니다. 이를 위해선 다시 인터뷰를 통해 MVP와 관련된 가설을 검증하는 고객발굴 활동을 수행해야 합니다.
모든 혁신 선도 기업들이 위 활동을 수행하는 만큼, 본 교과목을 통해 고객발굴 & 린스타트업 방법론을 학습/이해하시면 향후 여러분이 실무 활동에서 가치 창출을 이끌 혁신적 기업가(Innovative Entrepreneur)로 거듭날 수 있습니다.
수강자 여러분께서는 한 학기 동안 저와 증거 기반 기업가정신 활동을 수행할 것입니다. 자, 이제 우리와 함께 기업가적 여정(Entrepreneurial Journey)을 떠나 볼까요?

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
1. 강의 목표 :
광고는 마케팅의 핵심 커뮤니케이션 활동 중 하나입니다. AI 기반 빅데이터 분석과 다양한 정보 기술이 광고의 효과를 획기적으로 높이고 있습니다. 본 수업은 실제 기업들이 포스팅하는 소셜미디어 이미지 광고에서 효과적인 컨텐츠를 찾아내는 방법 및 새로운 광고를 생성하는 최신 연구들을 소개합니다. 구체적으로,
• 다양한 산업 분야에서 효과적인 광고 컨텐츠 예제
• 광고 컨텐츠 (예: 소셜 미디어)에서 다양한 시각적, 문자적 정보를 추출하는 AI 기술 (예: Google Vision)
• 수많은 컨텐츠 변수들 중에서 효과적인 변수를 골라내기 위한 데이터 분석
• 효과적인 광고 컨텐츠에 관한 가설 수립 및 검정
• 이미지 생성기 (image generator) 활용한 새로운 광고 콘텐츠 생성(예: Midjourney, Canva)
• 광고 분석 결과를 효과적으로 커뮤니케이션 하기
• 광고 컨텐츠 지식 생성과 관련한 윤리, 지식 재산에 관한 이슈

• Python 개요

3 ~ 4주:
• 광고 색깔 전략 – 화장품 (바디샵, DHC), B2C vs B2B 기업, AI 인플루언서 사례
• 광고 프레이밍 전략 – 기후 변화 사례
• 회귀 분석 개요
5 ~ 6주:
• 광고에서 다양한 시각적, 문자적 정보 추출 (Google Vision)
• 수많은 컨텐츠 변수들 중에서 효과적인 변수 골라내기 위한 다중공선성 (Multicollinearity) 진단 및 처리
7 ~ 8주:
• 효과적인 광고 컨텐츠에 관한 가설 수립 및 검정
• 가설 검증을 위한 변수 만들기 (예: 컨텐츠 사전)
• 사례: 패션회사들의 자연친화적 소셜미디어광고 (예: Awe 이미지) 분석
9 ~ 10주:
• 생성형 AI 활용한 big-tech 및 start-up 들의 신제품, 서비스 소개
• Midjourney, Canva 등의 이미지 생성 AI 활용한 광고 이미지 제작
• 디자이너, AI, AI-디자이너 협력 광고 비교
• 여러개의 이미지 혼합 (blending)하여 광고 생성
• 광고 컨텐츠 지식 생성과 관련한 윤리, 지식 재산에 관한 이슈
11 ~ 12주:
• 광고 컨테츠 내에서 효과적인 조합 (예: 슬픈얼굴 x 기쁜 메세지) 탐색
• 회귀 분석 – 조절 (Moderator) 변수
13 ~ 14주:
• 통합 마케팅 커뮤니케이션: 광고 컨텐츠와 제품/브랜드 포지셔닝과의 일관성 평가
• 사례: 바디샵 소셜미디어 광고
• 광고 컨테츠 갭 분석 (As-is vs To-be)
15 ~ 16주:
• 최신 광고 컨텐츠 전략 소개
• 인플루언서 광고
• 비쥬얼 스토리 광고
• 비디오 광고

- This class is intended for students who are currently taking, or have already completed, General Chemistry.
- Completion of General Chemistry Lab I is a prerequisite for enrollment in General Chemistry Lab II.
- [Important] For General Chemical Experiment I, priority enrollment is given to new students from the Mueunjae School of Undergraduate Studies (MSUS). During the course application correction period, additional registration may be possible until the maximum quota of 38 students is reached. Please note that if first-year students do not take their assigned classes in the designated semester, it may be difficult for them to graduate on time. They may also be unable to enroll on the class in a later semester due to its limited capacity.
- [Important] Participation in experimental classes requires submission of both a consent form for class operations and a certificate of completion for the semester’s 6-hour online laboratory safety training course.
- Students are expected to review the experimental procedures and content in advance, and to enter the laboratory fully prepared for the day’s experiment. A quiz on the day’s experiment will be conducted before the experiment begins.
- All experiments are conducted individually by each student.
- Students must comply with all laboratory safety regulations and follow the instructions of the Instructor in charge, including those related to clothing requirements.
o 2:00–2:15 Quiz
o 2:15–2:30 Student presentation and comments
o 2:30– Experiment
Other Important Matters
- Consult the Instructor regarding any matters related to the class.
- In principle, changing to another day’s class is not allowed. If any changes are necessary, consult both your teaching assistant and the Instructor in advance.
- All announcements will be made via the PLMS
- Experiments are conducted individually.
- Class materials will be posted on the PLMS one to two weeks before each experiment. Students should download and prepare the necessary files and forms in advance, refer to them during the experiment, and use them for report preparation in the relevant class.
- Students are encouraged to review the booklet How to Prepare an Experimental Report, available in the “Writing Content” section of the campus Writing Clinic.
- Since the evaluation of experimental reports (Pre-Lab, In-Lab, and Final Lab) constitutes the majority of the total score, it is essential to prepare these reports thoroughly.
- Plagiarism is considered a serious academic offense. Any plagiarized report will receive a score of zero, and points will also be deducted from the Class Performance score.
- If a student’s grade is deemed insufficient for a Pass, the instructor may assign an additional task.

- [Important] For General Chemical Experiment I, priority enrollment is given to new students from the Mueunjae School of Undergraduate Studies (MSUS). Please note that if first-year students do not take their assigned classes in the designated semester, it may be difficult for them to graduate on time. - Students are expected to review the experimental procedures and content in advance, and to enter the laboratory fully prepared for the day’s experiment. A quiz on the day’s experiment will be conducted before the experiment begins.
- All experiments are conducted individually by each student.
- Students must comply with all laboratory safety regulations and follow the instructions of the Instructor in charge, including those related to clothing requirements.

No formal prerequisite. Introductory knowledge on classical and quantum mechanics, calculus, linear algebra, differential equation, and most of all, your heart on quantum mechanics
Course Overview & Teaching Methodology
This course is built on traditional theoretical rigor, active problem-solving, and modern computational visualization:
Blackboard Talk & Python Demos: Lectures are delivered on the blackboard to build a deep, step-by-step understanding of mathematical derivations and physical intuition. Wednesday classes complement these lectures with interactive Python demonstrations to visualize quantum mechanical phenomena.
Homework & Bi-Weekly Quizzes: Ungraded weekly homework problems from McQuarrie’s textbook serve as your primary study guide. Understanding these problems is key, as bi-weekly 25-minute quizzes are directly adapted from homework assignments.
Student-Led Presentations: Starting after the midterm, students take the chalk during the second half of Wednesday classes to lead concise, 10-minute blackboard presentations on specific derivations and physical mechanisms.
The syllabus for this lecture including detailed lecture plan and specifics on evaluation will be given in the first class meeting. Please contact the instructor in advance by email if you have any concerns before selecting this course.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: To give you sufficient background and familiarity with the basic concepts of quantum mechanics as it is applied in Chemistry. Main focuses on chemical bonding and structure and basic understanding of spectroscopic features of atoms and molecules.

Lecture
Level 400
G
english
A basic understanding of general chemistry and organic chemistry is recommended. Prior coursework in biology is helpful but not required.
This course will combine lectures with problem solving, discussion, and interpretation of biochemical and structural data. Fundamental biochemical concepts will be introduced through lectures and progressively connected to experimental observations and contemporary research. In the later part of the course, students will apply these concepts to analyze molecular mechanisms and research questions.
Lecture notes and related materials will be uploaded to e-Class before each class. Students are encouraged to review the lecture materials in advance. Selected biochemical problems, molecular structures, and research figures may be discussed during class. Active participation and scientific discussion are encouraged.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: This course introduces the fundamental principles of biochemistry, with an emphasis on understanding the relationships among molecular structure, chemical interactions, and biological function. Students will develop the ability to apply these principles to understand biochemical mechanisms and interpret experimental data, while connecting fundamental concepts to contemporary research.

- This class is intended for students who are currently taking, or have already completed, General Chemistry.
- Completion of General Chemistry Lab I is a prerequisite for enrollment in General Chemistry Lab II.
- [Important] For General Chemical Experiment I, priority enrollment is given to new students from the Mueunjae School of Undergraduate Studies (MSUS). During the course application correction period, additional registration may be possible until the maximum quota of 38 students is reached. Please note that if first-year students do not take their assigned classes in the designated semester, it may be difficult for them to graduate on time. They may also be unable to enroll on the class in a later semester due to its limited capacity.
- [Important] Participation in experimental classes requires submission of both a consent form for class operations and a certificate of completion for the semester’s 6-hour online laboratory safety training course.
- Students are expected to review the experimental procedures and content in advance, and to enter the laboratory fully prepared for the day’s experiment. A quiz on the day’s experiment will be conducted before the experiment begins.
- All experiments are conducted individually by each student.
- Students must comply with all laboratory safety regulations and follow the instructions of the Instructor in charge, including those related to clothing requirements.
Note: To register for the course, please follow these steps:
1. In principle, registration for classes must be completed on the same day as General Chemistry Lab I (approval from the Instructor is required for a change of class).
2. Regardless of the class hours posted on PLMS or POVIS at the time of registration, the class will be held from 2 pm to 6 pm on the relevant day of the week.
3. After registration, the number of students may be reorganized according to the number of students enrolled on the course.
4. Applications must be made during the course registration period or the course registration confirmation and correction period.
5. General Chemistry Lab II is a recommended subject for the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering.
6. Consult the professor in charge of all matters related to the course.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: Nanochemistry deals with syntheses of various nanomaterials and nanostructures and the characterizations thereof. This class intends to address fundamentals on syntheses and applications of nano-sized structures that include organics, semiconductors and metals. Vacuum Process WK8-9: Forces between molecules and nanostructures (Van Der Waals interactions in nanoscales) WK8-10: Synthesis and lithography- Semiconductor nanocrystal quantum dots- Metal nanoparticles and nano-structures- Fullerine, carbon nanotubes, and bucky balls- Organic nanomaterials- E-beam Lithography- Focused Ion Beam Miller- Soft Lithography- Contact Lithography- Plasmonic Lithography- Nanosphere Lithography WK11-15: Applications of nanomaterials - Properties and applications of semiconductor nanocrystal quantum dots- Nanoplasmonics- Lasers & Optical Communications- Optical Switches and Optical Computings- Nanostructured Electrical Devices- Electron transport phenomena in nanostructures- Magnetic properties of nanomaterials and nanostructures- SpintronicsWK16: Final exam

sourceOperatingSections.8. 강의진도계획:
Week 1: Introduction and The First Law 1
Chapter 1. Introduction: Temperature, absolute and gauge pressure, nature of work and energy
Chapter 2. The First Law: Energy balance for closed systems, state functions and path functions
Week 2: The First Law 2
Chapter 2. The First Law: Definition of enthalpy, steady-state energy balance for open systems
Mechanically reversible processes and work calculations
Week 3: Volumetric Properties of Pure Fluids 1
Chapter 3. Volumetric Properties: PVT behavior of pure substances, ideal gas equation of state
Virial equation of state and compressibility factor
Week 4: Volumetric Properties of Pure Fluids 2
Chapter 3. Volumetric Properties: Cubic equations of state including van der Waals, Redlich-Kwong, Peng-Robinson
Theorem of corresponding states
Week 5: The Second Law of Thermodynamics
Chapter 5. The Second Law: Introduction to the second law, macroscopic and microscopic definitions of entropy
Thermodynamic temperature scale, entropy changes of an ideal gas, the second law for open systems
Week 6: Thermodynamic Properties of Fluids 1
Chapter 6. Thermodynamic Properties: Fundamental property relations for pure fluids
Maxwell relations and the calculus of thermodynamics
Week 7: Thermodynamic Properties of Fluids 2
Chapter 6. Thermodynamic Properties: Concept and calculation of residual properties
Fugacity and fugacity coefficient for pure species

(4) Applications of AI in Chemical Engineering: A review of specific examples of how artificial intelligence is being applied in the field of chemical engineering.

Transport Phenomena
• The syllabus is subject to change depending on the progress of the class.
• Carbon Neutrality Focus: In Weeks 14 and 15, we will specifically discuss the separation challenges in Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR). This includes:
o Direct Air Capture (DAC): Adsorption/Absorption kinetics for ultra-low concentration CO2.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
1. Course Description
This course explores the fundamental principles of Mass Transfer, the backbone of chemical engineering, and its application to industrial separation unit operations. We will focus on designing and analyzing processes such as distillation, extraction, and absorption. A special emphasis is placed on modern challenges, including Battery Recycling and Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) from the atmosphere and oceans, leveraging the organic connection between transport phenomena and process design as presented in the Geankoplis textbook.
• Main Textbook: Christie John Geankoplis, Transport Processes and Separation Process Principles, 5th Edition.
2. Learning Objectives
• Understand the fundamental principles of mass transfer and the concept of diffusion coefficients.
• Design distillation columns and extraction processes using the Equilibrium Stage concept.
• Master the Kremser Equation and the principles of gas absorption/stripping.
• Apply advanced theories of Liquid-Liquid Extraction (LLE) to real-world industrial processes.
• Build a foundation in membrane separation, which is increasingly vital in modern polymer and bio-industries.
• Analyze emerging technologies: Direct Air Capture (DAC) and Ocean Carbon Capture using advanced separation principles.
sourceOperatingSections.4. 강의선수/수강필수사항: Transport Phenomena
sourceOperatingSections.8. 강의진도계획:
1 Introduction: Definitions of separation processes & Thermodynamic foundations
2 Mass Transfer I: Principles of molecular diffusion and convective mass transfer
3 Mass Transfer II: Estimation of diffusion coefficients & Mass transfer coefficients
4 Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium: VLE relationships and non-ideal solutions (Activity Coefficients)
5 Distillation I: Batch distillation, Flash distillation, and McCabe-Thiele Method
6 Distillation II: Column efficiency, Reflux ratio optimization, Multicomponent distillation
7 Absorption & Stripping: Gas absorption equilibria and Packed Tower design
8 Midterm Exam (Covers Weeks 1–7)
9 Mass Transfer in Columns: HTU/NTU concepts and column design via Kremser Equation
10 Liquid-Liquid Extraction I: Principles of LLE, solvent selection, and Triangular Diagrams
11 Liquid-Liquid Extraction II: Countercurrent multistage design & Battery Recycling Case Study
12 Leaching & Crystallization: Principles of leaching and mechanisms of crystal growth
13 Membrane Separation: Polymer membranes (RO, UF, NF) and selectivity
14 Adsorption & Ion Exchange: Isotherms; Direct Air Capture (DAC) using solid sorbents
15 Emerging Technologies Ocean Carbon Removal (Electrochemical/Membrane) & Nanoparticles
16 Final Exam (Focus on Weeks 9–15)
sourceOperatingSections.9. 수업운영:

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
(Approximately half of this course will be delivered by invited external experts. Therefore, we kindly ask for your understanding that a significant portion of the lectures will be conducted in Korean.)
Significant efforts have been dedicated to developing and improving new materials for lithium-ion batteries to meet the growing power and energy demands of mobile electronics and electric vehicles. However, the widespread adoption of large-format lithium-ion batteries remains limited due to high costs, safety concerns, and limitations in energy density and calendar life. Advanced materials processing techniques offer promising solutions to these challenges.
This course provides a comprehensive overview of key materials processing methods used in the fabrication of cathodes, anodes, and separators for lithium-ion batteries. To cultivate specialized professionals in the field of secondary batteries and reflect the needs of industry, the curriculum goes beyond basic principles to include instruction on battery materials, synthesis strategies, and cell assembly. In line with the goals of the Graduate Program for Battery-Specialized Universities, the course is designed to foster highly trained battery professionals by covering topics ranging from the fundamentals of secondary batteries to seminar programs delivered by experts actively working in academia and industry. Additionally, guest lectures (in Korean) by leading experts from academia and industry will offer insights into current issues and real-world practices in Korea’s secondary battery sector.

[Course Overview]
With the increasing significance of eco-friendly energy materials, there is a growing demand for a convergent understanding of analytical techniques to characterize materials and elucidate the mechanisms behind performance enhancement. Given the rising complexity of modern materials, an in-depth understanding through multi-dimensional analysis is essential. Accordingly, this course introduces undergraduate students in Chemical Engineering and related convergent disciplines to the current development of various energy materials and the practical application of characterization tools, focusing on their fundamental principles and operational scopes.
[Learning Objectives]
- Fundamental Principles: Grasp the core principles of various analytical techniques utilized for characterizing energy and environmental materials, specifically for hydrogen production, storage, extraction, utilization, and CO2 reduction.
- Technical Selection: Evaluate the strengths, limitations, and application ranges of each characterization method to select the most appropriate tools for specific research objectives.
- Integrated Interpretation: Develop the ability to synthesize diverse analytical datasets to achieve a profound understanding of material properties within the hydrogen economy and carbon capture frameworks.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
An algorithm is a procedure or method for solving problems that arise across a wide range of computing applications. However, algorithmic problems in these domains are rarely formulated in a mathematically well-established way; they often include application-specific details, most of which are nonessential auxiliary elements.
The goal of this course is to understand how to systematically formulate problems and, based on that, to learn how to design correct and efficient algorithms.
- The course begins with an introduction to algorithms and then covers five core algorithm design techniques. It also addresses computational complexity theory and advanced algorithms.
- In addition, through Project-Based Learning (PBL) problem-solving, students enhance their understanding of algorithms and their problem-solving skills by actively learning in teams: designing, implementing, and presenting algorithms for real-world problems.

Reasons you must not audit:
- Attending a lecture is not the same as mastering the material. Without assignments and exams, you may feel like you’re learning, but the knowledge rarely moves into long-term memory.
- Why do the heavy lifting of a course for free? If you’re doing the assignments and taking the exams, take the credit too.
Class format:
- Face-to-face classes will be held in the classroom.
Course materials:
- Lecture slides will be posted on the PLMS prior to each class.
- As there is no textbook and the material is abstract, note-taking during class is strongly recommended.
- This course covers many topics quickly. Pre-study will enhance your understanding and active participation in class. Use your class time mainly for Q&A.
Assignments:
- Biweekly programming assignments: These assignments require significant time and effort. Start early to avoid falling behind.
- Programming language: Assignments must be written in Python 3.x.
- Development environment: A UNIX environment (e.g. Linux) is recommended for development.
You must write up HWs and code by yourself. The following are considered to be honor code violations:
- Looking at the writeup or code of another student.
- Showing your writeup or code to another student.
- Discussing homework problems in such detail that your solution (writeup or code) is almost identical to another student's answer.
- Uploading your writeup or code to a public repository (e.g. github, bitbucket, pastebin) so that it can be accessed by other students.
- Looking at solutions from previous years' homeworks - either official or written up by another student.
When debugging code together, you are only allowed to look at the input-output behavior of each other's programs (so you should write good test cases!).
It is important to remember that even if you didn't copy but just gave another student your solution, you are still violating the honor code, so please be careful.
We periodically run similarity-detection software over all submitted student programs, including programs from past semesters and any solutions found online on public websites.
Anyone violating the honor code will get F no matter what.

Class format:

sourceOperatingSections.10. 학습법 소개 및 기타사항:
You must write up HWs and code by yourself. The following are considered to be honor code violations:
- Looking at the writeup or code of another student.
- Showing your writeup or code to another student.
- Discussing homework problems in such detail that your solution (writeup or code) is almost identical to another student's answer.
- Uploading your writeup or code to a public repository (e.g. github, bitbucket, pastebin) so that it can be accessed by other students.
- Looking at solutions from previous years' homeworks - either official or written up by another student.
When debugging code together, you are only allowed to look at the input-output behavior of each other's programs (so you should write good test cases!).
It is important to remember that even if you didn't copy but just gave another student your solution, you are still violating the honor code, so please be careful.
We periodically run similarity-detection software over all submitted student programs, including programs from past semesters and any solutions found online on public websites.
Anyone violating the honor code will get F no matter what.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
Today, computers are not just in boxes and data-centers; they are extensively interwoven with our physical life. They sense us, predict us, and empower us to do more, no matter when and where. In this light, this course is designed to help the students (1) broaden their views on computer science across our real life, (2) learn how fundamental computer science principles and technology are engineered to create our daily intelligent companions, and (3) develop interdisciplinary intellectual senses connecting computer science with other fields of study.
This course will cover the basic systems, technology, and real-life applications pertaining to mobile and ubiquitous computing. The technical pillars and applications include (but not limited to): human activity recognition & localization, smart homes, physical & mental healthcare, cyber-physical privacy, social computing & crowd computing in physical life, novel user interfaces, and mobile deep learning. The course will also include advanced issues to optimize mobile and ubiquitous computing systems’ latency and energy efficiency. Also, this course will refer to some historic research which influenced the birth of today’s commercial IoT devices the students may be familiar to, such as Nest learning thermostats, FitBits, and even commodity services such as WiFi localization, so that the students can learn from examples.
This course plans at least one guest lecture to be given by a mobile / wearable computing researcher from a renowned global research laboratory (or equivalent).
The course does NOT plan mid-term or final exams. Instead, the course will include a term-project, expecting the students to form teams and build their own ideas pertaining to mobile & ubiquitous computing.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
**Continuous computation**, which involves continuous data and operations, is fundamental to many areas of computer science such as machine learning and scientific computing. Common examples include evaluating mathematical functions (e.g., numpy.exp(x)) and computing derivatives of programs (e.g., jax.grad(f)).
This course introduces the **foundations** of continuous computation. It covers a broad range of topics, from basic computations (e.g., evaluating math functions) to advanced ones (e.g., computing derivatives). Students will learn how to perform these computations *correctly and efficiently on actual computers*.
In essence, this course serves as a **continuous** counterpart to an Algorithms course, a **computational** counterpart to a Calculus/Probability course, and a **foundational** counterpart to a Numerical Analysis course. Lectures will start from first principles and emphasize both *mathematical theory and computational methods*.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
Quantum physics is an important building block of modern science, but many students find it difficult to understand, partly because of the advanced mathematics it requires and partly because of its non-intuitive properties, such as the wave-particle duality and the uncertainty principle.
This course aims to provide a pedagogical introduction to important quantum physics with minimal use of advanced mathematics. Starting from the pre-quantum physics era, the discussion will proceed to introduce the de Broglie wave and the Schrodinger equation. The equation will be solved in a few pedagogical situations to familiarize students with various non-intuitive implications of quantum physics. The time evolution of wave functions and wave-function collapse due to measurement will be discussed, along with their implication for quantum teleportation. Orbital angular momentum and spin angular momentum will also be discussed.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: This course will provide the introduction to the the elementary particle physics. Course Content
1. Introduction and Python Basics
- Introduction to computing and programming.
- Installing Python and setting up the environment.
- Basic syntax and data types.
2. Input/Output, Memory, and Variables
- Understanding and using input/output functions.
- Memory concepts in Python: How variables and data are stored.
- Variable types and declarations.

- Defining and using functions.
- Modules and packages.
4. Control Structures
- Conditional and looping statements.
- Controlling program flow.
5. Data Structures
- Lists, tuples, dictionaries.
- Manipulating and managing data.
6. String Manipulation
- String functions.
- String formatting.
7. File Input/Output
- Reading and writing files.
- Exception handling.
8. Midterm Exam
9. Advanced Data Structures
- Sets, stacks, queues.
- Complex data structures.
10. Object-Oriented Programming
- Classes and objects.
- Inheritance and Method overriding
11. Advanced Object-Oriented Programming
- Operator overloading.
- Polymorphism.
12. Recursion and Algorithms
- Recursive thinking.
- Basic algorithms.
13. GUI Programming
- Using Tkinter.
- Developing user interfaces.
14. Utilizing Libraries
- Standard libraries.
- Numpy, Pandas, etc.
15. Review and Consolidation
- Review of learned content.
16. Final Exam

- Students are expected to be familiar with Python to understand the course. Note that we will use C/C++ for the main language but may draw analogy from Python for easy of explanation.

** Attendance policy **
(1) Arriving more than 15 minutes late will count as one absence.
(2) Three instances of being late will be counted as one absence.
(3) Unexcused absences may lead to disciplinary action:
- Grades will be reduced with each absence beyond four (e.g., from A to B).
- Accumulating eight absences will result in failing the course.
(4) There will be random check during the class. If you mark your digital attendance and then disappear later during the random check, it will count as 3 absences.
Homework
- Programming assignments will be released four times during the semester
- Need to start early otherwise can’t finish on time
Self-study
- Lectures may only cover the concepts without discussing the details
- The assignments and exams requires you to understand the details in the textbook
- Strongly recommend you to read out the textbook yourself
- Self-study is very important for you to succeed in this course and others

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: Data Structures is an essential area of study for computer scientists and for anyone who will ever undertake any serious programming task. This course deals with the fundamentals of organizing and manipulating data efficiently using clean conceptual models. Students study many of the important conceptual data types, their implementation, and analysis of their efficiency. Topics will cover algorithm analysis, lists, trees, priority queues, dictionaries (hash tables, balanced search trees), graphs, strings (tries, pattern matching), and sorting.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: The goal of this course is to introduce the design principles and implementation of modern operating systems. The course covers the fundamental concepts of operating systems, including process management, memory management, file systems, and I/O management, and explains how these components are designed and implemented in contemporary operating systems. In addition to the theoretical foundations, the course includes a series of comprehensive programming assignments and laboratory exercises designed to develop practical system programming skills in UNIX-like operating systems, such as GNU/Linux.

metadata.currentPlanHeader: 2026-Fall ST: Principles of Deep Learning (CSED490M-01) The course syllabus

sourceOperatingSections.3. Course Objectives:
This is an introductory deep learning course for computer science undergraduate students that comprehensively covers the mathematical foundations, architectural principles, and cutting-edge methodologies of deep learning—the core pillar of modern AI. Beginning with the fundamentals of machine learning, the curriculum explores core deep learning mechanisms in depth. Students will derive the backpropagation and gradient descent algorithms that form the bedrock of deep neural networks, and progress from CNNs and RNNs to the Transformer architectures powering today's state-of-the-art AI.
Breaking away from rigid theoretical instruction, this course will adopt a generative AI-based teaching and learning workflow to adapt flexibly to rapid technological paradigm shifts. Students will engage with frontline topics in industry and academia from diverse perspectives. Students will also implement and optimize real-world code using AI coding agents, and engage in real-time debates with AI on open-ended technical topics, equipping them with both theoretical depth and practical insight.
Students who successfully complete this course will achieve the following competencies:
- Mastery of Theoretical & Mathematical Principles: Clear understanding of the underlying mathematics in deep learning; ability to mathematically derive and explain forward and backward propagation in neural networks.
- Analysis of Modern Architectures & Trends: Ability to analyze core mechanisms of modern architectures (e.g., Transformers) and critically compare large-scale model scaling trends and advancing training algorithms from an engineering perspective.
- Advanced AI-Collaborative Implementation: Proficiency in designing core deep learning layers and training pipelines using "Vibe Coding" workflows (seamlessly integrating PyTorch with AI coding agents); ability to independently debug and optimize system bugs and performance bottlenecks.
- Critical Thinking & Technical Communication: Ability to logically critique the limitations of deep learning through discussions with peers and virtual AI panels; capability to clearly communicate complex technical concepts using visual and interactive elements.
sourceOperatingSections.4. Prerequisites & require:
While there are no formal prerequisites for this course, the following background knowledge is highly recommended:
- Foundational Mathematics: A basic grasp of high-school or introductory college-level calculus, linear algebra, probability theory, and statistics.
- Basic Programming Skills: Familiarity with Python syntax and basic programming logic.
- Basic Machine Learning Literacy: Familiarity with core concepts such as linear/logistic regression, training models, supervised learning, and regularization.
- AI Agent Prompting & Debugging Literacy: Experience of writing clear, structured instructions to guide an AI's behavior and being able to identify, troubleshoot, and fix common errors or unexpected outputs.

sourceOperatingSections.9. Course Operation:
- Standard Lectures: Foundational concepts and core principles will be delivered through standard academic lectures.
- Discussion Sessions: To foster critical thinking, each lecture will include a dedicated discussion session where students can engage with the topics and exchange ideas.
- Midterm and Final Examinations: There will be two comprehensive exams during the semester to assess the understanding of fundamental theories.
- Hands-on Experiments and Practical Skills using AI: The course will also offer hands-on practice sessions utilizing coding agents, and students will have to create a blog post and interactive playground, gaining hands-on experience in AI collaboration.
sourceOperatingSections.10. How to Teach & Remark:
- The curriculum is intended for undergraduates, while we also permit the participation of graduate students who wish to build their foundations in deep learning.
- Thus priority will be given to undergraduate students in case of over-enrollment.
- The discussion sessions will help you build a deep intuition through peer-to-peer exchange.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표: This course is an introductory subject in the fields of power grid control and operation, particularly focusing on electric energy generation and transmission/distribution. Electrical power systems and machines are the foundation of the modern economy. Electric power has become increasingly important as a way of transmitting and transforming energy in residential, commercial, industrial, military, and transportation uses. Numerous systems and machines have been, and will continue to be, developed for the conversion, delivery, and use of energy in electrical form. The growth of solar energy, wind energy, and other resources, combined with new trends such as electric and hybrid vehicles, also has a profound impact on global society. For undergraduate- and graduate-level students, this course emphasizes general aspects of electrical energy generation and distribution, microgrid infrastructure, renewable resources (e.g., wind and solar), and efficient load devices (e.g., electric vehicles and HVAC systems) in smart building. The class activity ranges from operation of large utility systems and microgrids to control of energy devices using microsensors (e.g., phasor measurement units). This course will be useful to students who pursue careers or research in electric power systems, smart grids, power electronics, and development or use of electric motors and generators.

(b) System Type
- Reference Tracking
- Disturbance Rejection

실험에 사용할 USRP와 LabVIEW, Spectrum Analyzer의 사용법을 익히고 이를 이용해 디지털 통신 시스템을 구현하면서 구성 요소의 역할과 필요성을 숙지합니다.
구현한 송수신기로 신호를 만들어 USRP를 통해 주고받으면서 무선 환경에서 설계한 통신 시스템이 실제로 어떻게 동작하는지 관찰 및 분석합니다.

[ENG] This course aims to help students master the fundamentals of communications and networks through hands-on experiments and lab sessions.
Students will familiarize themselves with the usage of USRP, LabVIEW, and Spectrum Analyzers, and understand the roles and necessity of various components by implementing a digital communication system.
By generating and exchanging signals via USRP using the implemented transceivers, students will observe and analyze how the designed communication system operates in a real wireless environment.
This course is cross-listed as NGCN302 (an elective for the Next-Generation Communication and Network Convergence Minor) and EECE443 (an elective for the Department of Electrical Engineering).

Weekly Progress Reports and Presentations: Each student must submit a progress report (PowerPoint presentation) by posting on the website no later than 12:00 PM on every Monday AND give a presentation to the class at every Monday meeting at C5, #103 at 2:00 PM. The weekly progress reports must include the following.
 Objective
 Weekly Progress
 Issues
 Plan
Design Notebook: Each student is required to maintain a design notebook. This notebook should be a record of all work done during the course of the design project. The design notebooks are very important for final evaluation.
Proposal: In the first two weeks, each student must meet and discuss with a design advisor, decide his/her own project topic and submit a proposal. In Monday class meeting of the third week, each student should give a presentation of a proposed research. Note that the proposal presentation should include whether the proposed project will be done in one semester or continued to the next semester for the Creative IT Design IV project. The PowerPoint slides must be posted on the website before the proposal presentation. A proposal (PowerPoint presentation) must include the following.
 Objective
 Significance
 Innovation
 Research Approach
 Milestone
 Expected Outcomes
Progress Review: At the mid-term period (see Schedule for the date), each student should make an oral PowerPoint presentation of their progress to date. The PowerPoint slides must be posted on the website before the progress review meeting.
Final Poster Presentation and Demo: At the CiTD demo day (see Schedule for the date), each student will make a poster presentation demonstrating their design project. A prototype demonstration, if appropriate, is highly encouraged.
Final Report: A final written report must be handed in after the final presentation.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
1. Understand human-centered design principles and explain how human needs, cognitive characteristics, behaviors, and contexts inform the design of interactive systems.
2. Investigate users and real-world contexts using appropriate qualitative and user-research methods, including interviews, observation, thinking-aloud protocols, stakeholder analysis, and personas.
3. Translate user insights into design requirements by identifying problems, stakeholders, interactions, user journeys, scenarios, and functional requirements.
4. Apply an iterative design process to move from problem discovery and definition to concept development, prototyping, evaluation, and refinement.
5. Design and evaluate interactive experiences by considering usefulness, usability, affect, and broader dimensions of user experience.
6. Explore emerging forms of human–AI interaction involving LLMs, AI agents, MCP, and Physical AI, and critically consider how these technologies can be incorporated into human-centered solutions.
7. Develop and communicate a working prototype that demonstrates a coherent connection among user research, design requirements, technological possibilities, and design decisions.

This course provides innovative analysis of devices and circuits in electronic engineering, which is fundamental for IT engineering students. This course covers the fundamental physics of devices with materials and interpretation methods of electronic circuits.
* Note: This semester, it is only available to undergraduate students in the Department of IT Convergence. Other students can take the class starting next semester.
이 교과목에서는 IT공학도로서 기본적으로 알고 있어야 하는 전자공학의 소자 및 회로의 전반적인 내용에 대해서 다룬다. 전자회로의 기초 개념과 해석 방법, 트랜지스터, 연산증폭기와 같은 중요 소자의 동작원리 및 디지털 논리회로를 다루고 전자소자 재료의 제반 특성, 빛과 물질의 상호작용, 반도체, 도체, 비등방성 물질, 비선형광학 물질의 구조와 특성에 대해 기초소자(Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, PN diode, BJT, MOSFET 등)를 바탕으로 기초이론과 개념을 가르치는 것을 목적으로 한다.
sourceOperatingSections.8. 강의진도계획:
- 1주: Introduction: what is electronics? / applications of electronics and electronic components
- 2~3주 : Semiconductor Device Physics
- 4주 : Diodes with circuit analysis techniques
- 5주 : Capacitor and inductor with analyzing transient circuit
- 6주 : Transistor biasing and transistor amplifier circuits
- 7주 : Midterm Exam
- 8~9주 : Field Effect Transistors
- 9주~10주 : Integrated circuit design with the BJT
- 11주~12주: Integrated circuit design with the MOSFET
- 13~14주 : The differential stage and OP amplifier
- 15주 : Basic Logic circuits (CMOS inverter, CMOS logic gates)
- 16주 :Final Exam

심리학은 인간의 마음과 행동을 과학적인 방법으로 연구하는 학문입니다. 본 강의를 통해 여러분은 다양한 심리학의 분야를 접하게 됩니다. 구체적으로는 우리가 어떻게 세상을 지각하고, 정보를 처리하며, 우리의 뇌가 어떻게 생각과 행동을 조절하고, 기억과 감정이 발생하는지, 아이들이 자라며 어떻게 세상을 이해하게 되는지 배우게 됩니다. 또한, 성격은 어떻게 구성되어 있고 경험과 감정이 어떻게 우리의 삶을 구성하게 되는지, 정신질환의 원인과 치료법에 대해서도 이야기할 예정입니다.

- 특정 선수과목의 이수 및 법학에 대한 특별한 사전지식을 요구하지 않음
- 본 수업은 민주적 법치국가의 시민(citizen)으로서 기본소양을 갖추기 위한 목적을 가지므로, 매주 수업에서 다루게 될 주제들에 대한 폭넓은 관심이 있다면, 누구나 수강이 가능함
- 수강생들은 수업 전 담당교수가 지정한 참고문헌을 가볍게 읽고, 해당 내용에 대한 자기 나름의 생각을 정리하고 수업에 참여할 것을 권장함
- 청강은 (실제 수강생들의 수업권을 최대한 보장하기 위해) 특별한 사정이 없는 한 원칙적으로 불허함
- 수업 진행과정에서 수강생들과의 협의를 통해 구체적인 수업계획은 수정 및 보완될 수 있음

- 본 강의는 법학입문(Introduction to Law)에 해당하는 것으로, 법에 대한 기초적 이해를 다루는 교육과정을 제공합니다. 이는 민주적 법치국가의 시민으로서 기본적으로 갖추어야 할 법이해에 초점을 맞추어, 헌법상 기본권, 민법과 형법의 기본원칙, 시민불복종운동(저항권), 인권운동, 공익운동 등 현대 민주주의 사회의 제도적 장치, 나아가 ‘법과 정의’와 관련된 다양한 이론 및 사례 등을 통해 법의 근본문제를 이해하고 법적 사고능력을 배양하는데 도움을 주고자 합니다.

sourceOperatingSections.8. 강의진도계획:
[1주차] 수업 오리엔테이션, 시민교육으로서 법교육(1): 법의 이해
- 도덕, 관습, 예절, 법 등 사회규범과 구별되는 법의 규범적 특성
- 법의 기본적인 분류체계(사법, 공법, 사회법 / 실체법, 절차법)에 대한 설명
[2주차] 시민교육으로서 법교육(2): 법원과 재판
- 권력분립의 원칙 및 견제와 균형
- 헌법의 목차(입법부→행정부→사법부)가 갖는 함의와 국민주권
- 공식적인 분쟁해결방법으로서 재판
- 조정 및 중재 등 대체적 분쟁해결(ADR)의 법적 수용
- 재판의 종류와 민사재판 및 형사재판의 차이
[3주차] 시민교육으로서 법교육(3): 민사재판
- 민사재판의 개념 및 유형
- 사례를 통해 바라보는 민사재판의 절차
- 단독재판부와 합의재판부의 차이
- 민사재판과 당사자주의(처분권주의 및 변론주의)
- ADR의 법적 수용으로서 민사조정과 그 의의 및 한계
[4주차] 시민교육으로서 법교육(4): 형사재판
- 형사재판의 개념 및 유형
- 사례를 통해 바라보는 형사재판의 절차
- 형사절차에 따른 신분 개념과 인권적 함의
- 형사재판의 원칙(죄형법정주의, 무죄추정의 원칙, 적법절차의 원리 등)
- 체포와 구속의 유형 및 피의자의 권리
- 국선변호인 제도
- 사법접근권과 국민참여재판
- 소년보호재판과 소년법 관련 쟁점의 이해
[5주차] 시민교육으로서 법교육(5): 심급제도
- 사법권의 독립과 법원의 역할
- 법원의 종류 및 조직과 심급제도
- 상소(항소, 상고) 및 항고 개념의 구별
- 상고제도 관련 사법정책적 쟁점의 이해
- 우리나라의 전자소송과 ODR 관련 최근 논의 추이
[6주차] 법의 임무(1): 법과 정의
- 현대사회에서 법제화와 법의 도구화
- 국가법의 배후로서 시민법
- 법의 이념으로서 정의, 합목적성, 법적 안정성
- 현대사회에서 정의기준의 불확정성과 정법의 불확실성
[7주차] 법의 임무(2): 국가의 기본원리 – 민주적 법치국가
- 하버마스의 대화원칙에서 법질서의 의미
- 민주적 법치국가의 내적 통합과 인권과 주권의 변증
- 민주적 법치국가의 성찰적 기제로서 시민운동의 보완기능
- 민주적 참여의 확대로서 보충성원칙의 구현
[8주차] 중간고사 기간
[9주차] 법의 기초(1): 계약과 법
- 계약의 구속력의 근거로서 약속과 신뢰의 상호성
- 보편적 법규범으로서 사정변경원칙
- 계약의 자유와 그 제한의 근거로서 사회적 연대성
[10주차] 법의 기초(2): 손해의 전보와 법
- 정의의 실현 및 자유보장의 기획으로서 손해전보제도
- 국가배상책임의 발전 및 최근 동향
- 민사책임과 형사책임의 분화
- 손해전보요건의 구조: 고의/과실, 손해야기행위, 위법성, 인과관계, 손해의 발생
- 현대사회에서 책임귀속원리의 변형으로서 위험책임 및 무과실책임
[11주차] 법의 기초(3): 헌법과 기본권 보장
- 대한민국 헌법의 구성
- 헌법 전문(前文; preamble)의 의미
- 헌법상 기본권과 열거되지 않은 기본권
- 기본권 제한의 법리로서 과잉금지원칙
- 위헌법률심판제청과 헌법소원
- 2018년 헌법 개정안에 대한 소개 및 비판적 검토
- 헌법재판소법의 개략적 소개
*** 헌법재판소 대표 결정문 검토 및 분석 ***
- 공직선거법 제15조 위헌확인(헌재 2013. 7. 25. 2012헌마174): 선거권 행사 연령을 19세 이상으로 정하고 있는 공직선거법 제15조 제1항이 19세 미만인 사람의 선거권 및 평등권을 침해하는지 여부
- 집회 및 시위에 관한 법률 제10조 등 위헌제청(헌재 2014. 3. 27. 2010헌가2 등): 해가 뜨기 전이나 해가 진 후의 시위를 금지하는 집회 및 시위에 관한 법률 제10조 본문 중 ‘시위’에 관한 부분이 집회의 자유를 침해하는지 여부
- 형법 제241조 위헌소원 등(헌재 2015. 2. 26. 2009헌바17 등): 배우자 있는 자의 간통행위 및 그와의 상간행위를 2년 이하의 징역에 처하도록 규정한 형법 제241조가 성적 자기결정권 및 사생활의 비밀과 자유를 침해하여 헌법에 위반되는지 여부
- 형법 제269조 제1항 등 위헌소원(헌재 2019. 4. 11. 2017헌바127): 임신한 여성의 자기낙태를 처벌하는 형법 제269조 제1항, 의사가 임신한 여성의 촉탁 또는 승낙을 받아 낙태하게 한 경우를 처벌하는 형법 제270조 제1항 중 ‘의사’에 관한 부분이 헌법에 합치하는지 여부

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
This course develops linear algebra through a simplified approach emphasising applications to machine learning and statistics centered subjects via the cross-filling method (rank-one decomposition) that simplifies traditional Gaussian elimination with boarder applications to other application areas.
Covered topics include:
• Matrix computation strategies: Cross-filling, sum ↔ product equivalence
• Vector spaces and subspaces: Null space, column space, the four fundamental subspaces
• Projection theory: Oblique and orthogonal projections, compatible families, spectral decompositions
• Determinants: Axiomatic properties, Laplace expansion, Cayley-Hamilton theorem
• Eigenvalues and spectral decomposition: Lagrange interpolation approach to diagonalization
• Normal matrices and applications: Hermitian/unitary matrices, positive definiteness, singular value decomposition (SVD)
Applications include:
• Multi-variable Linear Regression and Data Analysis
• Differential Equations
Pedagogical note: This curriculum uses cross-filling and Lagrange interpolation as primary computational methods, offering alternative and often more elegant techniques than traditional approaches.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
There are two big topics in Linear Algebra; one is solving a system of linear equations, and the other is the eigenvalue and eigenvector. We understand these two topics by understanding vector spaces and linear transformations, and hopefully learning the domain and codomain of a linear transformation can be decomposed into the four fundamental spaces. These concepts are summarized as the Singular Value Decomposition Theorem.
More specifically, we will study
* vector space and matrix, linear system
* PA=LU decomposition
* four fundamental spaces
* rotations in 2D and 3D
* orthogonality and projections
* least square method
* determinant
* eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization
* matrix powers and matrix exponential
* Jordan normal form
* positive definite matrix and congruence
* Singular Value Decomposition

Course Format: The class will be a mixture of lecture and discussion. I expect you all to show up having read the assignment for that meeting and ready to use it as a point of departure. It is the nature of the issues we will be considering that people’s views will differ. You are encouraged to question your classmates (and me) when anyone says something you disagree with, but everyone should always keep in mind that disagreement is not a personal attack.
General Information and Policy
1. Disability: If you have a disability that may require assistance or accommodation, or you have questions related to any accommodations for testing, note-takers, readers, etc., please speak with your instructor as soon as possible.
2. Make-up Policy: You can take a make-up exam if (1) you have such a conflict as a religious observance, a University-sponsored event you participate in that takes place at the exam time, or any medical reasons; (2) you provide me with relevant evidence such as a doctor’s note.
3. Presence: You can sign on a paper sign-in sheet only if you are present in class. Asking implicitly or explicitly anyone other than you to sign in for you is cheating. In case you find your name box on a sign-sheet filled by someone else, you must let me know immediately. Anyone who intentionally puts anything in a box that contains the name of another student is committing cheating. If you cheat once on presence/absence management, you will get an F and the incidents will be reported to the University.
4. PLAGIARISM: No student shall submit the words, ideas, images or data of another person as the student’s own in any academic writing, essay, thesis, research, project or assignment in a course or program of study. That means that you have to cite all your sources. If you don’t, you get 0 on the assignment (and maybe the course, depending on how serious it is), and a letter from the university office. Handing in an identical paper to another student is also considered plagiarism. So take it seriously. If you’re having a problem with an assignment, or if you aren’t sure whether something is plagiarism, come see me and I’ll help you to do it properly.
5. EXTENSIONS: Extensions will not be given simply because you didn’t plan well enough. Plan ahead, and save yourself problems. A late assignment will be accepted without any penalty if there is an exceptional reason for the work to be late, including such things as illness, might be accepted with some penalty in some situations, or may not be accepted in some cases. However, I highly encourage you to talk with me if you want to make up for any missing assignment.
6. Collaboration: You may collaborate with your classmates for solving problems that are not hw questions. However, you should not discuss with other people about any hw problems, nor show your hw answers to others, nor compare your answers with others’ before submitting your final work – by others I mean not just students taking this class but any people. You ought not to use any materials you have acquired from other people to do hw assignments. The final work to be submitted must be your own one. Anyone who does not abide by these rules will get an F and the incidents will be reported to the University.

The goal of this course is twofold: (1) to provide an introduction into the workings of financial markets and (2) to analyze the role of financial markets for the broader macroeconomy. The course will discuss the basic role of financial markets, the types of financial assets, and how they are traded. We will introduce a number of technical tools for valuing risk, pricing financial assets, and constructing investment portfolios. Finally, we will apply these insights to examine issues of broader macroeconomic relevance, with special emphasis on current financial challenges and crises.
In addition to this core framework, the course aims to equip students—especially those from science and engineering backgrounds—with the following competencies:
- Comprehensive Understanding of Financial Instruments and Markets: Students will gain foundational knowledge of asset classes, market mechanisms, and institutional structures that drive global finance.
- Analytical Skills for Investment and Valuation: The course covers key topics such as risk-return tradeoffs, portfolio theory, bond pricing, and derivative valuation, enabling students to assess investment opportunities rigorously.
- Integration of Finance and Macroeconomics: Students will explore how financial markets interact with macroeconomic variables, including interest rates, inflation, and economic growth.
- Quantitative and Technical Proficiency: Leveraging their STEM training, students will apply mathematical, statistical, and computational tools to solve real-world financial problems and interpret market data.
By the end of the course, students will be well-prepared to approach complex financial and economic issues with a structured, analytical perspective—laying the groundwork for future work in finance, technology, data science, or policy.

- No specific prerequisites are required to take this course.
- An interest in interpersonal and social influence, and a curiosity about social scientific experimental research design.
1. Students will study persuasion topics (see the course schedule) grounded in social scientific research methods, primarily lab and field experiments involving human subjects. The course also reviews empirical studies that have tested various persuasion theories, with attention to how the "conclusions" drawn on different persuasion topics were actually arrived at. This course will be particularly useful for students interested in conducting usability tests with human subjects in the future.
2. Students will examine actual experimental studies on persuasion and practice critically engaging with their underlying assumptions, theoretical logic, methodology, and alternative interpretations of the findings.
3. This course will differ from what students might expect if they assume it covers the kind of self-help books on persuasion commonly found in bookstores (e.g., "secrets" or "tricks" of persuasion). Students should keep in mind that this course approaches persuasion from a scientific and ethical standpoint.
4. Persuasion is distinct from manipulation, propaganda, inducement, and coercion. This course focuses on persuasion grounded in an ethical approach.
5. The course consists of the instructor's lectures, quizzes, group presentations by students, discussions, and occasional in-class worksheets.
- Instructor's lectures + real-world examples + Q&A session
- Actively applying course concepts to the writing assignment (individual work)
- Applying theoretical concepts to analyze persuasive strategies in science video content (group work)

3. To develop the competencies of an effective and strategic communicator.

* Course Description: Industrial organization is a field that stems from Microeconomics. It is interested in imperfect competition with few competitors. The less competitive market structure creates situations with strategic interactions among the market participants. The course will explore competitive and cooperative strategies employed by profit maximizing under a variety of market structures when there are few firms, entry barriers, differentiated products, and/or imperfect information.
* Course Objectives/ Student Learning Outcomes: Upon completion of this course, students will:
1. Be able to understand theoretical principles of strategic behaviors under different a wide range of market structure
2. Be able to discuss such strategic behaviors in the context of real-world examples
3. Be able to develop their own strategic approaches based on such understanding of markets structure and market situation
4. Be able to answer how market economy contributes to economic growth with innovation.

이 교과는, 학생들이 긴 분량의 텍스트를 제대로 읽어내는 고급 문해력을 향상하고 이를 바탕으로 제반 사회 상황을 역사적, 사회적으로 잘 이해할 수 있도록 하는 데 목적을 둔다. 구체적으로는 (1) 우리 시대에 한층 중요해지는 읽기의 의미를 이해하고 심층 독해 방법을 습득한 뒤에, (2) 학문 제 분야의 다양한 텍스트들을 직접 독해해 봄으로써 (3) 인간과 사회에 대한 심도 있는 이해력을 확보할 수 있게 한다.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
The purpose of this course is to help students learn that scientific ideas can be precisely formulated with mathematical languages , that science is a source of mathematical ideas that profoundly shape the development of mathematics, and that mathematics can furnish brilliant answers to important scientific problems.
For example, why do we consider the "numbers" ? Where can we employ them ? In fact, numbers are scalars and, in real (industrial or experimental) life, may symbolize the objects as energy, distance, density, temperature, and so on. Eventually, we formulate scientific problems with mathematical languages and can solve, provide well-organized algorithms for the problems.

Level 400
G

본 수업은 기술과 몸의 문제를 사회학적인 시각과 과학기술학적인 시각으로 풀어가는 과목으로 강의와 발표로 결합되어 운영될 것이다.

sourceOperatingSections.3. 강의목표:
지식탐구역량강화 (50%); 창의융합역량강화 (50%)
최근 문제가 되고 있는 생명윤리 문제, 과학과 여성, 기타 과학사 관련 이슈 과목을 과학기술학 특강의 형태로 개설한다. 특히 이번 과학기술학 특강은 “몸의 사회적 의미와 관리”와 “새로운 유전학의 대상으로서 신체” 그리고 “새로운 생명정치학과 신체”라는 세 가지 주제를 다루게 될 것이다.

제 1주: The return of the body – Introduction
Freund, Peter E.S. 1988. “Bringing Society into the Body: Understanding Socialized Human Nature.” Theory and Society 17-6: 839-864.
Lock, Margaret. 1993. “Cultivating the Body: Anthropology and Epistemologies of Bodily Practice and Knowledge.” Annual Review of Anthropology 22: 131-55.
Chris Shilling. 2007. Sociology and the Body: Classical Traditions and New Agendas. Sociological Review. 55(1). 1-18.
Featherstone, Mike, Mike Hepworth, and Bryan S. Turner (eds.). 1991. The Body: Social Processes and Cultural Theory. Newbury Park: Sage Publications.
Foster, Susan (ed.). 1995. Corporealities: Body, Knowledge, Culture, Power. London:
Routledge.
제 2주: Categorizing Bodies: Sex, Gender and Sexuality
Fausto-Sterling, Anne. 2005. “The Bare Bones of Sex Part I: Sex and Gender.” Signs 30(2):1491-1527.
Kessler, Suzanne. 1990. “The Medical Construction of Gender: Case Management of Intersexed Infants.” Signs 16(1): 3-26.
제 3주: Habitus and the social body
Marcel Mauss. 1935/1973. “Techniques of the Body.” Economy and Society 2: 70-88. Reproduced in Beyond the Body Proper, edited by Margaret Lock and Judith Farquhar.
Pierre Bourdieu. 1984. The Habitus and the Space of Lifestyles in Distinction: A Social Critique of the Judgement of Taste.
Philippe Bourgois and Jeff Schonberg. 2007. “Intimate Apartheid: Ethnic dimensions of habitus among heroin injectors.” Ethnography. 8(1): 7-31.
Recommended:
Bourdieu, Pierre. [1980] 1990. The Logic of Practice, Preface, Book I, esp. “Belief and the Body,” and chapter 3 of Book II, “The Devil of Analogy.”
Loic Wacquant. 1995. Pugs at Work: Bodily Capital and Bodily Labor Among Professional Boxers. Body and Society 1-1 (March): 65-94.
제 4주: Regulating bodies – Foucault’s panopticism, Biopower and the ethics of the self
Foucault, Michel. 1980. “Body/Power,” pp. 55-62; “The Politics of Health in the Eighteenth Century,” pp. 166-182; “The History of Sexuality,” pp. 184-194 in Power/Knowledge: Selected Interviews and Other Writings 1972/1977. Edited by Colin Gordon. New York: Pantheon.
Foucault, Michel. 1984. “Docile Bodies,” “The Means of Correct Training,” and “Panopticism,” in The Foucault Reader. Edited by Paul Rabinow. New York: Pantheon, pp. 179-213.
Recommended
Foucault, Michel. 1975. Discipline and Punish: The Birth of the Prison (Part One, chapter one, “The Body of the Condemned,” Part Three, chapter one, “Docile Bodies,” and chapter two, “The Means of Correct Training.” If you can manage it, also read, Part Three, chapter three, “Panopticism.”).
Lois McNay. 1991 ‘The Foucauldian body and the exclusion of experience’ Hypatia 6 (3): 125-139
제 4주: Displaying and Modifying bodies: cosmetic surgenry

Kathy Davis (1995). Reshaping the Female Body: The Dilemma of Cosmetic Surgery. NY:Routledge.
Kathy Davis (1997). “My body is my art,” in K. Davis (ed.), Embodied Practices: Feminist Perspectives on the Body. Thousand Oaks CA: Sage,
Kathryn Pauly Morgan (1992) ‘Women and the knife: cosmetic surgery and the colonization of women’s body’ Hypatia 6(3): 25-53
제 5주: Consumption and the Body
Mike Featherstone and Roger Burrows (1995) Cyberspace/Cyberbodies/Cyberpunk –special issue of Body&Society 1(3-4).
Anthony Elliott (2008) Making the Cut. How cosmetic surgery is transforming our lives London: Reaktion Press, chs 3,4.
Lori Andrews and Dorothy Nelkin (2001) Body bazzar: the market for human tissue in the biotechnological age, New York: Crown Publishers
제 6주: Masculine Body
Rosalind Gill, Karen Henwood and Carl McLean (2005) ‘Body projects and the regulation of normative masculinity’ Body &Society 11(1): 37-62.
Sally Sheldon (2002) ‘The Masculine Body’ in Mary Evans (ed) Real Bodies, Basingstoke: Palgrave, ch. 2.
제 7주: Medicalized Bodies, Bodies at Risk
Nicholas Rose. 2001. The Politics of Life Itself. Theory, Culture & Society. 18(1). 1-30.

제 8주: The Making of Biological Facts
Ian Hacking. 1986. Making Up People. Reproduced in Beyond the Body Proper, edited by Margaret Lock and Judith Farquhar.

제 9주: Biosocialities

제 10주: New biopolitics
Paul Rabinow (1996) Essays on the Anthropoloy of Reason, Princeton: Prince

Nicholas Rose (2006) ‘Biopower today’ BioSocieties 1(2): 1-12
Nicholas Rose (2007) The politics of life itself: Biomedicine, Power and Subjectivity in the Twenty-first Century, Princeton: Princeton University Press
제 11주: New biopolitics and its assessment
Esposito, R. (2008) Bios: Biopolitics and Philosophy (Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press)
Cooter, R. & Stein, C. (2010) ‘Cracking biopower’ History of the Human Sciences 23 (2): 109-128
Cooter, R. (2007) ‘After death/after life: the social history of medicine in post-postmodernity’ Social History of Medicine 20 (3): 441-464.

Cooter, R. (2008) ‘Biocitizenship’ Lancet 372 (15 November 2008): 1725.
